record.paper_title: Progress and open questions in the physics of neutrino cross sections at intermediate energies
record.original_question: What form factors and higher-order corrections are needed to describe neutral-current photon emission from nucleons and nuclei at higher energies in a way that respects unitarity, given that the relevant form factors are poorly understood and contact-term or loop effects can modify the amplitudes substantially?

evidence.quote: The extension to higher energies requires the introduction of poorly understood form factors...

However, one should recall that this trend will be limited by unitarity bounds: in a realistic framework, these amplitudes will be modified by loop contributions and partially canceled by contact terms of even higher orders.
However, as discussed in Sec. IV D 2 in the nucleon case, the results are not only highly sensitive to unknown form factors but should also be constrained by unitarity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the process of neutral-current (NC) photon emission off nucleons and off nuclei induced by neutrino scattering, mediated by the exchange of a Z boson, with an outgoing real photon and an outgoing nucleon (or nuclear final state). At low energies the amplitude can be organized in a chiral effective field theory expansion in which baryon resonances (in particular the Δ(1232), as well as higher N* resonances) are included as explicit degrees of freedom and the relevant electroweak transition currents are parameterized by vector and axial form factors of the nucleon and of the N → resonance transitions. As the neutrino energy increases beyond the regime where the leading tree-level chiral/resonance expansion is reliable:

(a) Identify the complete set of electroweak transition form factors (nucleon vector and axial form factors, as well as N → Δ and N → N* vector and axial transition form factors at the relevant momentum-transfer range) whose Q²-dependence must be specified in order to describe NC single-photon emission amplitudes at intermediate-to-high neutrino energies, and determine which of these form factors are presently constrained by independent data (electroproduction, pion photo- and electroproduction, parity-violating electron scattering, etc.) and which are unconstrained.

(b) Determine the higher-order corrections — including contact terms of higher chiral order, meson-loop contributions, and rescattering/final-state interactions — that must be incorporated so that the resulting amplitude for NC photon emission satisfies the unitarity bounds (e.g., partial-wave unitarity of the γ N → γ N and the related coupled-channel S-matrix) in the kinematic region where individual tree-level resonance contributions would otherwise grow without bound.

(c) Construct an explicit theoretical framework (for both the single-nucleon amplitude and its embedding into a nuclear many-body calculation) that simultaneously (i) incorporates these form factors, (ii) implements unitarization (e.g., via Bethe–Salpeter / K-matrix / N/D resummation of loop and contact contributions), and (iii) reduces, in the appropriate low-energy limit, to the known chiral effective theory result.

Specify the form factors, the higher-order operators and loop topologies, and the unitarization scheme required, and show that the resulting amplitude is consistent with unitarity throughout the intermediate-energy region relevant to accelerator-based neutrino experiments.
artifact.status_search_result: NC single-photon emission off nucleons and nuclei remains an active area of theoretical study, with several groups (Hill; Wang, Alvarez-Ruso, Nieves; Rosner; Zhang & Serot) extending chiral/effective-field-theory treatments and including resonance and unitarization effects, but a complete treatment that fixes all required form factors and enforces unitarity at intermediate energies has not been established. The problem is generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino- and antineutrino-induced single-photon emission
status_evidence.snippet: Extending the model to higher energies requires the inclusion of additional resonances and form factors that are poorly known, and unitarity must be respected.
status_evidence.claim: The community acknowledges that form factors and unitarization at higher energies for NC photon emission remain an open theoretical issue.

status_evidence.title: Low energy analysis of νN → νNγ in the Standard Model
status_evidence.snippet: Hill's effective theory analysis is restricted to low energies; extension upward requires unknown form factors and higher-order operators.
status_evidence.claim: Effective-theory treatments are limited to low energy and a unitarity-respecting extension is not available.
